info.title: Qwen Managed Agent Public and WebShell API
info.description: Canonical first-release contract for the public Managed Agent resources and the WebShell adapter. Implemented routes and fields describe the current matching Server, Broker, Harness and WebShell build. Partial entries have remaining implementation or contract-test work; planned entries are not current server capabilities and must be excluded from production SDKs. Turn submission and cancellation always return the durable operation identifier and its persisted admission and delivery state. Session-list cursors are bound to the normalized archive state and title query. Earlier development API shapes, checkpoints and database catalogs are unsupported; initialize fresh state for this build. Runtime feature capabilities and deployment policy still govern optional execution modes. Public conversation history reads directly from mutable message projections; persisted conversation snapshots and fixed-content paging are no longer provided. Retained removed MCP-management entries stay in the response snapshot: only non-removed entries count toward the 32-server selection capacity, so the servers array may exceed 32 while preserving tombstones.

post.description: Stores revision 1 of a new tenant-scoped definition under a server-generated agent ID. The same Idempotency-Key with the same body replays the original revision; a different body answers 409 idempotency_conflict. Sessions may be created from a stored definition by agent_id (v1.41): an explicit agent_revision pins that revision, an omitted one resolves the latest at admission, and permission_policy, tools, model and instructions then take effect for that Session (model must be on the deployment's agent-model allowlist, the tool profile on its tool-profile allowlist); content that cannot take effect yet is refused at admission with 409 agent_definition_unsupported.

202.description: Immutable agent revision published.

get.description: Reads the latest revision, or the one named by revision. An unknown agent ID or revision answers 404 agent_not_found.

200.description: Requested or current agent revision.

post.description: Stores the next immutable revision. Content whose digest equals the latest revision stores nothing and answers with that revision. The same Idempotency-Key and request replay the recorded revision. If another update takes the same next revision number, the losing write answers 409 agent_revision_conflict without recording its key, so that key can be retried. The returned revision may be superseded by a concurrent update before the response arrives.

202.description: The next immutable revision, or the latest revision unchanged when the submitted content digest already equals it; no revision is appended in that case.

post.description: Workspace selection is persisted with the original actor-scoped creation receipt. With the deployment's G0 file admission opt-in, qwen-code Sessions in an authorized, preregistered Workspace may include initial input under the server-selected profile, and a Session pinned to a stored definition may include initial input when its single tools entry selected a profile from the deployment's definition tool-profile allowlist. Otherwise Workspace creation must have empty input. Newly bound qwen-code Sessions, including empty creation, persist hosted-workspace-shell/1 with mandatory default/auto-edit approval when the Shell deployment opt-in is enabled; otherwise they persist hosted-workspace-files/1 with the configured file approval mode. The switch does not override a stored AgentDefinition's compiled profile or approval mode. Public callers cannot select the built-in profile. Any caller holding the OPERATOR role may submit later Turns and rename the Session under the same opt-in, while the Workspace registry row stays ACTIVE and still backs the binding, the actor recorded by the Workspace create command keeps OPERATOR or above, and the Session is active and undeleted and is either a qwen-code Session on the frozen execution profile or pinned to a stored definition; Workspace close follows its separate close capability and lifecycle admission; the same caller may cancel a running Turn (its delivery re-checks no grants); archive and unarchive follow their separate retention capabilities after reliable Workspace close; delete supports idle ACTIVE Sessions through their admitted Workspace lifecycle protocol, including v2 Shell/MCP, or reliably CLOSED/ARCHIVED Sessions; directory-change submission is retired; previously admitted durable cwd_change operations remain queryable and continue settling. This surface has no per-caller capability flag for later Turns, so callers must handle a refused later Turn — 403 session_operation_forbidden below the role and 409 workspace_unavailable past it, or 404 session_not_found without Workspace read. Check replay before resolving defaults; a durable binding is not proof of Runtime readiness. A stored AgentDefinition may be selected by agent_id: an explicit agent_revision pins that revision, an omitted one resolves the latest revision at admission and pins it for the Session's life, an unknown agent or revision answers 404 agent_not_found, and definition content that cannot take effect yet answers 409 agent_definition_unsupported with error.field naming the refused field. Shell Sessions additionally require the Shell opt-in and valid persisted approval for fresh Turns; disabling only Shell admission preserves original-key replay and accepted approvals and cancellation while Workspace files remain enabled and persisted approval remains valid. Qualified new public Shell Sessions expose agent by default under the public-child deployment switch and runtime/Harness admission; existing Sessions retain their original tool scope. Invalid approval or files-off can refuse attachment. Public Shell close and active delete require lifecycle v2 and reliable original-Worker stop support; archive and unarchive require completed close proof.

delete.description: Unbound Sessions accept active, closed or archived state. Returns 409 turn_active while a Turn is active and session_operation_active while another lifecycle change is pending. The same key from the same actor returns the original operation, also after the Session was deleted. Workspace-bound ACTIVE deletion supports idle hosted-workspace-files/1 Sessions when L3 lifecycle protocol and reliable Runtime stop are available. Only the Session's recorded owner (owner_actor_key, with the pre-V40 creator fallback) with current read access may admit it; accepted, running, cancelling or approval-waiting Turns return 409 turn_active. Admission persists a lifecycle-only execution fence and a versioned actor-scoped operation. SessionEnd settles before SessionDelete; committed Hook results are verified in Session Store and saved before permanent draining, attachment cleanup and original worker stop. Unknown outcomes or missing original stop evidence remain recovery_blocked and are never replayed on a replacement worker. CLOSED/ARCHIVED deletion retains L2: completed reliable-close evidence is required and no Harness or Hook is invoked. Completion atomically commits retirement, tombstone, receipt and terminal event, retaining shared Workspace files and neighboring holders. Authorized same-actor/key replays return the original operation, including after deletion; a readable non-owner returns 403. Missing lifecycle capability or close evidence returns 409 workspace_unavailable.

202.description: Deletion accepted. The Session stops accepting input and reads deleting. For a supported ACTIVE Workspace files Session, SessionEnd and then SessionDelete settle under L3 before permanent draining and verified original Runtime stop; CLOSED/ARCHIVED Workspace Sessions use independent L2 retirement. Unbound Sessions retain their existing lifecycle flow. Completion leaves a tombstone: Session reads return 404, while its operations stay readable. The shared Workspace is never deleted, and no Session content is erased yet. 202 does not mean that tools have stopped.
Input or cancellation durably accepted.

get.description: Returns JSON by default. Accept text/event-stream or stream=true to receive SSE. Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. A cursor strictly below replay_floor_sequence gets 409 cursor_expired as JSON; SSE sends one agent.session.resync_required frame and closes. Projection rebuilds preserve the floor and invalidate message-page cursors. Reload current Items after the projection catches up; expired event positions do not become readable again.

get.description: Requires current Session read authorization on every page. Read bounded current message-table pages in chronological order. The first request fixes a sequence membership upper bound; later pages retain that range but read current bodies and statuses. Numeric after excludes every Item with first_sequence at or below that value. Explicit cursor takes precedence; nonnumeric after is an existing cursor alias. Continuation uses the complete (first_sequence,item_id) position. Cursors bind tenant, Session, direction and projection generation, and are rejected after a projection rebuild. post.description: Synchronously rename a Session in one local SQL transaction under the same authorization as public PATCH. The public SQL row is the display authority: HTTP 200 confirms the SQL title is persisted, while the Harness journal copy is updated by a best-effort notification after commit and may lag or be skipped when the Harness is unavailable or does not support fenced titles. Workspace-bound fresh renames require current OPERATOR access and the original binding's execution facts; unbound Sessions use the existing tenant-scoped rename authorization. An active Turn does not itself block rename. Reuse the same idempotency key only for the same Session and title; completed replay returns the Session's current persisted title without another notification, including the existing last-visible result after deletion. Fresh-rename capability changes do not preclude authorized replay. The result title is authoritative and can differ from the requested title when a later rename already completed.

200.description: Authorized durable resource view; no Runtime startup required.

Tasks of this Session, newest first (created_at descending, then id descending), merged from the record domains the server projects — Monitor runs today, the others arrive with their stages. Settled tasks stay listed. The projection is rebuilt from durable domain records, so task IDs and order survive a restart. A task.updated Session event, with data.taskId and data.state, announces each change of a task's view.
Current task view, including settled tasks. 404 task_not_found covers tasks outside the caller scope.

Task events strictly after the cursor, oldest first, published as a committed prefix per task: no event may become visible at or before any previously returned event, page or output_cursor position. 400 invalid_event_cursor rejects a malformed cursor or one from another task. The durable retention floor is the position after the newest expired event, initially the stream start; only an oldest prefix expires. 409 cursor_expired means strictly below that floor, even when no events remain; equality is valid. Its replay_floor_sequence and snapshot_through_sequence stay absent because task cursors are opaque. Cursor identity, logical position, payload and accepted schema/projection versions survive rebuilds, restarts and archival; retention may still expire a cursor. Any output-producing task requires capabilities.artifacts. An output event holds back its own expiry and every later event until its full text is durably readable in an Artifact and discoverable by subsequent recovery reads, including through a potentially lagging task projection. Time retention is a target under healthy archival, not an unconditional deletion deadline. Archival failure pins the floor; H3 must bound durable backlog and apply producer backpressure and admission blocking before capacity is exhausted, or leave output-producing tasks disabled. Never silently discard accepted output. After cursor_expired, read one event page from the floor without after and save next_cursor; do not wait for has_more=false because an active producer may never catch up. Then read a fresh task view and discover/read its Artifacts, then resume from the saved page cursor, including events held back by the first page limit, not the new view's output_cursor. If the floor overtakes the reader, restart recovery; never treat another 409 as an empty page. Until older Artifacts can be enumerated and attributed to the task, H3 must prevent rotation beyond the 100 artifact_refs entries; afterward recovery must also enumerate older Artifacts. Recovery is guaranteed while the task and its Artifacts remain readable under their retention and authorization rules. Stage H3 defines stable output segments for joining Artifacts and events without overlap. 400 unsupported_feature when the Session does not serve tasks (capabilities.tasks is false).

202.description: Java durably accepted the cancellation and owns delivery; 202 does not prove owner acceptance or physical stop. After the tenant/actor filter and request decoding, validate Idempotency-Key (missing: 400 invalid_request; malformed: 400 invalid_idempotency_key), then current access (404 for an unreadable Session/task, then 403 task_forbidden for a readable task the actor may not cancel), then idempotent replay. The domain is tenant/session/operation-kind/actor/key; the digest includes task_id and excludes trace-only request IDs. While the record is retained and access remains valid, the same key and digest returns the same operation with its latest durable state and replayed=true; another digest returns 409 idempotency_conflict. Only new requests check capabilities.tasks (400 unsupported_feature), then Session active state (409 session_not_active otherwise, including closing, closed, archived and deleting), then action_capabilities containing cancel (409 task_action_unavailable otherwise), then, for a Workspace-bound Session, no storage migration fence (409 workspace_unavailable otherwise, as the sibling bound admissions answer). Admission requires no other open operation on the Session: cancel operations share the durable operation table with the lifecycle commands, which admit one open operation per Session, so any open operation answers 409 session_operation_active and an open cancel blocks close, archive and delete the same way. Atomically recheck admission and create the operation, serializing with Session/task transitions; a concurrent same-key winner replays before new-request state checks. trustedTenant.name: X-Qwen-Tenant-Id
trustedTenant.description: The tenant scope of the request. In the gateway topology it is injected by the trusted authenticated gateway and never trusted from browser input; in signed mode (qwenSignature) the broker authenticates it as part of the signed header set.

trustedActor.name: X-Qwen-Actor-Id
trustedActor.description: Verified actor identity. In the gateway topology it is injected by the authenticated gateway together with tenant and browser-supplied headers are stripped. In signed mode (qwenSignature) the broker authenticates it as part of the signed header set. Resource ACLs are mandatory in either mode; Action responder eligibility resolves to the Session's recorded owner or a Workspace OPERATOR, except a Shell Session, which only its recorded owner may answer and falls back to the tenant scope when neither an owner nor a create command was recorded. This header is not a browser credential.

qwenSignature.name: X-Qwen-Signature
qwenSignature.description:
Gateway-free authentication. The caller sends X-Qwen-Tenant-Id, X-Qwen-Actor-Id, X-Qwen-Signature-Timestamp (epoch seconds, within the server drift window) and X-Qwen-Signature: v1=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256> over "qwen-broker-auth-v1
" + METHOD + "
" + request path (undecoded, without the query string) + "
" + raw query string (empty when absent) + "
" + tenant + "
" + actor + "
" + timestamp + "
" + lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw request body + "
" + the Idempotency-Key header value (empty when absent), keyed by the server signing key. A missing actor, signature or timestamp header answers 401 authentication_required (a missing tenant header answers 400 invalid_tenant from the tenant filter); a stale timestamp or wrong signature answers 401 invalid_signature. Applies to every covered public and WebShell route, including the bare POST /v1/agents collection route and normalized path spellings. X-Qwen-Tenant-Id, X-Qwen-Actor-Id and X-Qwen-Signature-Timestamp are all mandatory alongside X-Qwen-Signature; an apiKey scheme names a single header by specification, so the other three are declared here in prose rather than as separate schemes.

TaskEventCursor.name: after
TaskEventCursor.description: Opaque task event cursor: an event cursor, a page next_cursor or a task output_cursor. Omit it to read from the durable retention floor. Strictly below the floor is 409 cursor_expired; equality is valid, including with no retained events.

IdempotentReplay.description: True when an accepted command or operation was replayed for the same idempotency key and digest without repeating its mutation. Session mutation responses represent the recorded outcome on the Session as last visible — a rename or unarchive replay after delete answers with the Session's pre-delete status rather than 404, while a create replay after delete answers 404 on the public create route, which re-reads the Session before responding, and answers the recorded 202 admission carrying the tombstoned sessionId on the WebShell create route, which does not re-read it; operation responses represent the original operation at its current state.

RequestId.description: Trace-only correlation identifier; never an idempotency key.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated actor belongs to another tenant than X-Qwen-Tenant-Id or has an invalid ID (actor_scope_mismatch, which the tenant filter answers on every /v1/agents/ and WebShell route), or the resource is readable but the actor lacks this operation or the original Action responder permission. Artifact content reads may also return artifact_content_forbidden when the actor cannot read the original bytes.

Unauthorized.description: A trusted actor is required for this request but none was supplied (actor_required). In signed authentication mode (qwenSignature) every covered public and WebShell route additionally answers 401 authentication_required when the signature, timestamp or actor headers are missing, and 401 invalid_signature when the signature is wrong or stale.

PayloadTooLarge.description: In signed authentication mode (qwenSignature) a request body beyond the configured signed-body limit (qwen.managed-agent.auth.max-signed-body-bytes, default 10 MiB) answers 413 payload_too_large before the signature is compared.

Conflict.description: State, idempotency, or recovery conflict. New Workspace-scoped admissions return workspace_unavailable with retryable=false while an offline Workspace migration holds the storage fence; authorized durable replays retain their existing behavior.

NotFound.description: Resource absent or outside the caller tenant scope.

CursorExpired.description: Replay cursor is older than the retained replay floor.

TaskCursorExpired.description: Task event cursor is strictly below the task's durable retention floor, which survives an empty retained set; equality is valid. The envelope's replay_floor_sequence and snapshot_through_sequence stay absent because task cursors are opaque.

Unavailable.description: A dependency such as the Hosted Harness is unavailable; retry later.

MessageProjectionChanged.description: 409 message_projection_changed: the message projection generation changed. Discard the message cursor and restart this read; this is not replay-floor cursor expiration.

MessagePageTooLarge.description: 413 message_page_too_large: selected message bodies or Turn control events exceed the response byte budget. Reducing limit can help a multi-Item page, but a single oversized Item cannot be returned even with limit=1. Signed POST requests may also return payload_too_large when their request body exceeds the configured signed-body limit.

InvalidMessagePage.description: 400 invalid_message_cursor for malformed, wrong-scope, wrong-direction or out-of-range message cursors; invalid_limit outside 1..100; invalid_event_cursor for a negative numeric after.

MessageProjectionPending.description: 503 message_projection_pending: projection coverage is below the replay floor, or the initial forward read is behind committed events. Retry after message projection catches up.

catalog_revision.description: The pinned catalog revision; null while no catalog has been published.

SessionModelConfig.description: Immutable Session connection. Requires session-model-config/1, encrypted storage and an endpoint in the control-plane allowlist. UTF-8 limits: model 512 bytes, base_url 2048 bytes, api_key 4096 bytes, complete canonical JSON 8192 bytes. Secrets are never returned in public Session responses. Child Sessions inherit the configuration. Cannot be combined with modelId.

base_url.description: Exact allowlisted HTTP(S) base URL without userinfo, query or fragment.

agent_revision.description: Optional explicit revision; omitted resolves the latest revision at admission and pins it. For the built-in qwen-code agent it must equal the deployment revision.

input.description: Text has a 4,000,000-character aggregate budget and per-block 1,000,000-character cap, counted in code points. Hosted also enforces its 64 KiB durable-record limit for text-only inputs and a 32 MiB prepared-snapshot ceiling. A complete canonical input containing file/image attachments must fit within 8 MiB and requires input-attachments/1.

stream.description: Phase one requires false; stream through the events route.

workspace.description: W0. Only omission allows default resolution; null or an empty object is invalid. Resolve and persist an explicit authorized tenant default on first admission; no default means workspace_required. The caller request digest retains an omission marker; replay resolves the original receipt before defaults. A changed default must never rebind a retry. Unavailable W0 support rejects rather than ignores this field.

skills.description: Optional static Skills imported from the enabled management catalog or added explicitly to the pinned AgentDefinition catalog. The merged catalog has unique names, at most 256 entries, 512 KiB per body and 2 MiB compact JSON. Requires session-skills/2; persisted immutably and included in creation idempotency.

extensionPins.description: Optional immutable initial extension selection. Omission keeps the legacy configuration path; an explicit empty array starts the unified configuration format. Included in creation idempotency and applied before the first model request. Requires session-extension-packages/1 and an extension-capable original Runtime.

worktree.description: Opt into a main Session worktree on supported LOCAL storage. Omission uses the current directory; an empty object freezes HEAD at first admission. Requires an explicit Workspace. Preparation is durable and gates Runtime execution; replay preserves the original commit, directory and branch.

memory_store_id.description: Optional immutable binding to the authenticated user's personal MemoryStore. Omission disables long-term memory. Bound Sessions require owner access as well as existing Workspace grants; creation idempotency includes this field.

input.description: Text has a 4,000,000-character aggregate budget and per-block 1,000,000-character cap, counted in code points. Hosted also enforces its 64 KiB durable-record limit for text-only inputs and a 32 MiB prepared-snapshot ceiling. A complete canonical input containing file/image attachments must fit within 8 MiB and requires input-attachments/1.

title.description: The server enforces the bound in UTF-16 code units (Java String.length()), so an astral character counts as two: a title this schema's code-point maxLength accepts can still exceed the server's 256-unit bound and answer 400 invalid_title.

admission_stage.description: Persisted admission stage of the operation.

delivery_state.description: Current delivery state of the operation.

agent_digest.description: Digest of the pinned stored AgentDefinition revision (D8b); absent for the built-in qwen-code agent.

replay_floor_sequence.description: Events at or below this sequence may be pruned. A replay cursor strictly below this durable floor has expired, including after projection rebuild or removal of every retained event. Reload current Items to resynchronize; projection coverage below the floor returns retryable message_projection_pending.

snapshot_through_sequence.description: Retained wire name for current message projection coverage; no persisted conversation snapshot is implied.

workspace.description: Absent for unbound legacy records, whose execution stays blocked pending evidence-based migration. Ready means committed context, not an active Runtime gate.

compaction_revision.description: Sequence of the most recent native context.compacted event; independent of Workspace context revision. Omitted when retained pre-upgrade evidence cannot establish the revision, and context compression is unavailable.

context_compression_operation_id.description: Current durable context compression operation, including recovery_blocked; absent when none is active.

memory_store_id.description: The personal MemoryStore selected at creation; absent when memory is disabled.

owner_only.description: When true, only the owning actor with existing Workspace grants may access this Session. Private children inherit visibility without inheriting the Store binding.

snapshots.description: Retained capability name for reading the current message projection. It does not promise persisted fixed-version conversation snapshots.

session_lifecycle.description: True when the Session accepts close, archive and delete operations; false for a Workspace-bound Session.

session_close.description: Deployment support for close independently of archive/delete; bound files Sessions require durable worker stop support. This is not actor authorization: admission also requires Session ownership and current read access.

session_archive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

session_unarchive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

session_delete.description: Optional support capability. ACTIVE Workspace files Sessions require L3 lifecycle protocol and reliable original Runtime stop; CLOSED/ARCHIVED Sessions use independent L2 close evidence. Current creator/read authorization and idle/source-state admission checks still apply. The aggregate session lifecycle capability is unchanged.

foreground_shell.description: Present only for persisted Shell Sessions, with no schema default; files and unbound Sessions omit it. True when Workspace files, Shell deployment admission and persisted default/auto-edit approval are valid. False prevents fresh sending. Disabling only the Shell flag preserves accepted cancellation and approval while Workspace files remain enabled and persisted approval remains valid; files-off or invalid approval can refuse attachment. This capability does not override authorization or recovery refusals.

context_compression.description: Requires a compatible Hosted Harness and an active Workspace Session. WebShell also reflects the current caller OPERATOR or OWNER grant; admission separately checks idle state.

child_agents.description: Public child orchestration support for this persisted Session. New launches also require current deployment admission; existing task read, approval and cancellation remain independently authorized.

PublicEvent.description: A committed event, replayed with the versions and identity it was accepted with. A stream.reconciled event is the exception: it means that Harness recovery retracted earlier deltas of its Turn, which now have empty text and no item_id or content_part_id, and that later deltas may name other Parts. Start a fresh Items query and retry message_projection_pending until the returned snapshot_through_sequence reaches the stream.reconciled sequence. Resume after that returned sequence, which bounds the initial live-message membership range; content is not frozen.

SessionResyncRequired.description: Data of the agent.session.resync_required SSE frame. Read the Session and its Items, then resume after the snapshot_through_sequence that the Items list returns; the value in this frame can be older.

snapshot_through_sequence.description: Retained wire name for current message projection coverage; no persisted conversation snapshot is implied.

created_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, Turn, Event and Item resources report.

skills.description: Stored revision content remains open to future options. Null or [] is the same as omitting the field. At Session admission only AgentStaticSkill shapes are supported, at most 16 with unique names and a Workspace tool profile; the compact UTF-8 JSON resource must not exceed 49152 bytes. Skill permissions, hooks, model overrides and other fields are refused at admission.

mcp_servers.description: Stored revision content remains open to future options. Session admission supports AgentMcpServerPin shapes: 1-16 unique Runtime-provisioned server pins without recipes or credentials on explicitly allowlisted hosted-workspace-mcp/1 or hosted-workspace-shell/1. The legacy MCP profile requires nonempty pins; pins are optional on ordinary Shell, which retains Read/Write/Edit, Shell and file backups/rewind. Shell with MCP requires the Hosted workspace-shell-mcp/1 feature and Shell lifecycle v2 capability. Plan is explicitly unavailable with nonempty MCP pins. Other profiles, foreground-only SSH and dedicated CSI resident execution do not support these pins. Public close requires compatible lifecycle v2 support.

hook_catalog.description: Stored revision content remains open to future options. At Session admission only the AgentHookCatalogPin shape is supported: a Runtime-provisioned catalog identity, requiring a Workspace-bound tool profile, without recipes or credentials. Null is the same as omitting the field.

archiveState.description: Filter before pagination. Omission preserves all readable, undeleted Sessions. Cursors are bound to the normalized archive state and title query.

titleQuery.description: Case-insensitive literal title substring, with surrounding whitespace stripped. Empty means no title filter; %, _ and backslash are literal. Applied before pagination. modelId.description: Optional host-catalog model for a bound built-in qwen-code Session. Requires modelSelectionSupported. Persisted atomically before the first Turn and included in creation idempotency; omission preserves the default model and old digest.

title.description: The server enforces the bound in UTF-16 code units (Java String.length()), so an astral character counts as two: a title this schema's code-point maxLength accepts can still exceed the server's 256-unit bound and answer 400 invalid_title.

input.description: Text has a 4,000,000-character aggregate budget and per-block 1,000,000-character cap, counted in code points. Hosted also enforces its 64 KiB durable-record limit for text-only inputs and a 32 MiB prepared-snapshot ceiling. A complete canonical input containing file/image attachments must fit within 8 MiB and requires input-attachments/1.

approvalMode.description: Optional initial execution policy for Workspace creation, validated against the resolved Agent and profile. Omission preserves its default and idempotency digest. Independent of planMode.

planMode.description: Persisted public Plan overlay, independent of execution permission. Omission on a change preserves the selected state.

skills.description: Optional static Skills imported from the enabled management catalog or added explicitly to the pinned AgentDefinition catalog. The merged catalog has unique names, at most 256 entries, 512 KiB per body and 2 MiB compact JSON. Requires session-skills/2; persisted immutably and included in creation idempotency.

extensionPins.description: Optional immutable initial extension selection. Omission keeps the legacy configuration path; an explicit empty array starts the unified configuration format. Included in creation idempotency and applied before the first model request. Requires session-extension-packages/1 and an extension-capable original Runtime.

worktree.description: Opt into a main Session worktree on supported LOCAL storage. Omission uses the current directory; an empty object freezes HEAD at first admission. Requires an explicit Workspace. Preparation is durable and gates Runtime execution; replay preserves the original commit, directory and branch.

memoryStoreId.description: Optional immutable binding to the authenticated user's personal MemoryStore. Omission disables long-term memory. Bound Sessions require owner access as well as existing Workspace grants; creation idempotency includes this field.

input.description: Text has a 4,000,000-character aggregate budget and per-block 1,000,000-character cap, counted in code points. WebShellMetadata.description: Arbitrary caller metadata, as a JSON object (or null). Accepted and ignored in Phase 1: nothing from it is persisted. operationId.description: Durable operation identifier for turn submission or cancellation.

admissionStage.description: Persisted admission stage of the operation.

deliveryState.description: Current delivery state of the operation.

WebShellAdmission.description: Command admission. Session creation and internal commands may omit operation fields.

status.description: recovery_blocked with hosted_harness_recovery_blocked means the Harness stopped without a safely settled Turn. The input remains active internally. Execution redispatch is parked, while bounded read-only observation of the original Harness journal may settle a later terminal result. Policy changes and lifecycle close wait for settlement; explicit cancellation remains available.

creationOperationId.description: Original create_session operation; creation retries resolve this identity before allocating another Session.

snapshotThroughSequence.description: Retained wire name for current message projection coverage; no persisted conversation snapshot is implied.

approvalMode.description: Current effective approval policy; initialApprovalMode retains the immutable creation policy.

initialApprovalMode.description: Immutable creation-time policy, used to confirm creation replay.

planMode.description: Persisted public Plan overlay, independent of execution permission. Omission on a change preserves the selected state.

planModeSupported.description: Optional deployment capability; missing means false.

compactionRevision.description: Sequence of the most recent native context.compacted event; independent of Workspace context revision. Omitted when retained pre-upgrade evidence cannot establish the revision, and context compression is unavailable.

contextCompressionOperationId.description: Current durable context compression operation, including recovery_blocked; absent when none is active.

lifecycleOperation.description: Current unsettled lifecycle operation, queried in batch under Session read authorization. A failed close/delete may leave the Session closing/deleting; only explicit retry starts a new operation. Settled Sessions omit this projection.

cwdChange.description: Retired: Session directory-change submission has been removed; always false.

workspaceTurns.description: True when the caller may submit later Turns of this Workspace-bound Session: the deployment enables Workspace files, the caller holds the OPERATOR role on a Workspace registry row whose state is ACTIVE and still backs the Session's binding, the actor recorded by the Workspace create command keeps OPERATOR or above, and the Session is active and undeleted and is either a qwen-code Session or a Session pinned to a stored definition (both on the Workspace's frozen execution profile). Cancelling only aborts work already running, so an OPERATOR caller may cancel a running Turn even when this is false; the capability does not gate cancellation. False for every other caller and for unbound Sessions, which do not use it. Shell Sessions also require foregroundShell=true for fresh sending; workspaceTurns may remain true with Shell admission disabled and is not sufficient Shell Turn admission. Manual rename uses the independent rename capability.

sessionClose.description: Close support including current actor authority. Workspace-bound Sessions require the recorded Session owner and current read access. Source-state and idle admission remain authoritative on the server.

sessionArchive.description: Archive support including current actor authority. Workspace-bound Sessions require completed reliable-close evidence, the recorded Session owner and current read access. Source-state and idle admission remain authoritative on the server.

sessionUnarchive.description: Unarchive support including current actor authority. Workspace-bound Sessions require completed reliable-close evidence, the recorded Session owner and current read access. Source-state and idle admission remain authoritative on the server.

sessionDelete.description: Delete support including current actor authority. ACTIVE Workspace Sessions require a supported reliable-close protocol; CLOSED/ARCHIVED Sessions use completed close evidence. Workspace-bound Sessions require the recorded Session owner and current read access. Source-state and idle admission remain authoritative on the server. The aggregate session lifecycle capability is unchanged.

foregroundShell.description: Present only for persisted Shell Sessions, with no schema default; files and unbound Sessions omit it. True when Workspace files, Shell deployment admission and a valid persisted approval mode are valid. False prevents fresh sending. Disabling only the Shell flag preserves accepted cancellation and approval while Workspace files remain enabled and persisted approval remains valid; files-off or invalid approval can refuse attachment. This capability does not override authorization or recovery refusals.

modelChange.description: The caller may change the Session model selection for later Turns using the server model catalog, including while a Turn or approval is active. Missing means unsupported; authorization, recovery and revision admission still apply.

approvalModeChange.description: The caller owns this eligible Workspace Session with current OPERATOR or OWNER access. Built-in qwen-code requires approval-selection/1; stored AgentDefinitions on exactly hosted-workspace-files/1, hosted-workspace-files/3 or hosted-workspace-shell/1 also require agent-definition-approval-selection/1. Idle-state admission is checked separately. Missing means false.

inputAttachments.description: Optional deployment capability; missing means false.

rename.description: True for a visible ACTIVE Session when the Harness supports fenced title persistence and is available. Workspace-bound Sessions additionally require Workspace files admission, current OPERATOR access and the original binding's frozen execution facts, independently of approval or fresh Turn sending support. Unbound Sessions use the existing tenant-scoped rename permission. An active Turn does not itself make this false. Missing means false. This advertises fresh rename only; authorized completed original-key replay remains available under the rename service's replay rules.

contextCompression.description: Requires a compatible Hosted Harness and an active Workspace Session. WebShell also reflects the current caller OPERATOR or OWNER grant; admission separately checks idle state.

childAgents.description: Public child orchestration support for this persisted Session; launch and caller authorization are checked separately.

diagnostics.description: Passive persisted context, model statistics, resource inventory and direct child invocation queries are available. Each response declares its observation coverage independently of Runtime readiness or fresh Turn admission.

coveredSequence.description: Actual message projection coverage of this read; resume SSE after this sequence.

lastSequence.description: Actual message projection coverage for SSE handoff, equal to coveredSequence; unmaterialized tail events are delivered by SSE.

WebShellEvent.description: A committed event, replayed with the versions and identity it was accepted with. A stream.reconciled event is the exception: it means that Harness recovery retracted earlier deltas of its Turn, which now have empty text and no itemId or contentPartId, and that later deltas may name other Parts. Reload the transcript and resume after its lastSequence.

WebShellResyncRequired.description: Data of the agent.session.resync_required SSE frame. Reload the transcript, then resume after its lastSequence.

snapshotThroughSequence.description: Retained wire name for current message projection coverage; no persisted conversation snapshot is implied.

retryable.description: Present on Runtime Broker refusals; true permits retry, false is a definite refusal. Other errors may omit this field.

field.description: Names the definition field that cannot take effect on 409 agent_definition_unsupported; other errors may omit this field.

WorkspaceRelativePath.description: Logical directory relative to the authorized workspace root; dot denotes root. Use slash separators. Reject absolute paths, drive prefixes, backslashes, NUL and parent segments. Runtime must verify directory existence, realpath containment and symlink safety before activation; schema validation alone is insufficient. Preserve spaces and case, normalize repeated separators and dot segments, and never percent-decode JSON values.

can_create_session.description: Current actor permission hint only; creation rechecks ACL, state and Agent/config compatibility.

workspace_context.description: True only after W0 creation, binding and private installation contracts are supported end to end.

workspace_binding.description: Supports authorized Workspace discovery, Session creation, and saved binding read-back. This capability does not advertise execution readiness. task_id.description: Task that a task_cancel operation targets.

failure_code.description: Reason a durable response or task cancellation failed. Action response failures come from the original committed Action, or a definitive invalid response. Task cancel failures are task_already_settled (the run ended before the stop request was recorded), task_action_unavailable and task_not_found; a recovery_blocked task cancel reports task_cancel_unconfirmed. A lifecycle operation that exhausted its retry budget fails with the settle's failure: session_lifecycle_delivery_failed, managed_capability_mismatch or hosted_harness_protocol_error when the Hosted Harness refused to negotiate, a workspace close or lifecycle refusal (a workspace_close_* or workspace_lifecycle_* code, or runtime_admission_closed; a Runtime Broker runtime_broker_recovery_blocked refusal is reported as workspace_close_identity_unverified), or another Runtime Broker refusal code; one whose settle reached the Harness but stayed unsettled past the larger settled budget fails with session_close_completion_unsettled. A lifecycle recovery_blocked operation reports the refusal it waits on, original resource identity or unsettled execution for a Workspace close, session_close_writer_live while a Harness holds the journal writer or while that check itself fails, or hosted_harness_generation_mismatch while this replica's view of the Harness boot is stale, or hosted_lifecycle_recovery_required while the daemon settles a previous prompt, or hosted_turn_active while a turn, MCP call or hook is still draining; the Session remains closing. A submit_input failure carries its Turn's error code, and a recovery_blocked submit_input reports submit_input_unconfirmed; a cancel fails with turn_already_settled when its Turn completed or failed without being cancelled, except one that already existed when its Turn failed with managed_runtime_recovery_blocked after a Harness admitted it or a submission was attempted: it parks recovery_blocked with cancel_unconfirmed. A cancel submitted after the Turn ended still fails turn_already_settled. A cancel parked as recovery_blocked/cancel_unconfirmed by unobserved-Turn recovery reconciles only from the original prompt's retained durable terminal event: cancelled completes it, completed or error fails it with turn_already_settled, and missing or unreadable evidence stays parked. A recorded stop request alone does not prove cancellation completed.

PublicCommandOperation.description: Receipt IDs are opaque authorized product handles, not private journal or storage refs. A recorded stop request alone does not prove cancellation completed.

includeChildren.description: Include pending Actions of this public root Session and its direct children; each Action retains its actual owning sessionId.

requestId.description: Trace-only client request identity, excluded from idempotency digests.

TaskState.description: Logical run state. completed is terminal and is set when the run's own line ends settled, with or without a physical execution; failed and cancelled are terminal too, and they also cover a run that ended before its execution started (cancelled before dispatch, or failed with no provable start), when no physical execution ever settled. degraded means that the task still runs with reduced guarantees, such as a Monitor that lost its observation source. recovery_blocked means that recovery cannot prove the physical outcome: it is not settled, is never reported as success and is never re-run automatically.

TaskRuntimeState.description: Redacted state of the Runtime that hosts the task, without binding identity or generation.

TaskActionCapability.description: Actions the task supports now, the same for every caller. cancel: the cancel route accepts a new command for this task (since 1.40 for child_agent, 1.46 for workflow and 1.54 for background_shell and monitor, tasks of those kinds in pending, running, waiting or degraded, and since 1.57 for channel_delivery, a delivery still pending because no adapter has claimed it, each in an active Session, and since 1.65 for automation_run in pending, running, waiting or degraded in an active Session; only that occurrence is cancelled and its schedule is preserved); whether a caller may use it is an authorization check (403 on the cancel route). send_input: reserved for a later capability route. read_output: the task events route returns output events for this task to any caller that can read it. read_output does not change during the task's life, and a task without it produces no output events: its output goes only to Artifacts, so the events route never filters out events that exist.

child_session_id.description: The child Session that runs this task: present for a child_agent or workflow task once the run's committed record names it (the child's attach, or a terminal verdict that names a minted child), and absent for every other kind and before then. The child is a Session in the same Workspace, readable by exactly the callers that can read this task, so its Turns, items and events are the task's own output; reading them needs no other grant.

definition_revision.description: Immutable definition revision this run is pinned to, when the kind has a definition.

created_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

started_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

settled_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

output_cursor.description: Stable task event cursor after the committed tail at view read time. No event can later appear at or before it. Pass it as after to follow only new events; recovery must instead keep its saved event page cursor so it does not skip intervening output. Normal retention may expire it.

artifact_refs.description: The newest Artifacts that hold durable task output, at most 100, oldest first. Entries must not rotate out until older Artifacts can be enumerated and attributed to the task: an evicted Artifact stays readable by id through the Session artifact routes but is no longer discoverable from the task.

stop_requested.description: A durable stop request has been recorded. This does not prove that the task has terminated.

approval_mode.description: The actual immutable approval mode of this public child Session.

PublicTask.description: Read-only projection of one asynchronous task of a Session (SessionTaskView). It is rebuilt from the Session's durable domain records and is never their source of truth. It never carries a Runtime binding ID, generation, Runtime endpoint, Pod, absolute path, raw PID, SecretHandle or local sidecar; diagnostics are authorized Artifact references.

cursor.description: Stable opaque position after this event and its identity. Atomically apply the event and save this cursor to avoid duplicate application after a crash. It is never reassigned; normal retention can expire it.

truncated.description: True when the chunk was cut to the event limit; its full output is already durably readable and discoverable in the task Artifacts when the event is published.

PublicTaskEvent.description: One task event: a logical state change, a bounded output chunk, or an Artifact reference. High-volume output goes to Artifacts or bounded chunks in this paged stream, never one Session event per raw line. The closed schema validates the server's own version; clients ignore unknown optional fields and unknown types and checkpoint their cursors. Strict response validation against an older minor version is not supported. Event identity, position, payload and accepted schema/projection versions are immutable across restart, projection rebuild and archival.

childSessionId.description: The child Session that runs this task: present for a child_agent or workflow task once the run's committed record names it (the child's attach, or a terminal verdict that names a minted child), and absent for every other kind and before then. nextCursor.description: The last returned event cursor, never passing an event held back by limit. On an empty page, the requested position, or the durable retention floor if after was omitted. Required and never null, including when no events remain. No event may later become visible at or before this position.

after.description: Opaque task event cursor: an event cursor, a page nextCursor or a task outputCursor. Omit it to read from the durable retention floor. Strictly below the floor is 409 cursor_expired; equality is valid, including with no retained events.

requestId.description: Trace correlation only; excluded from the request digest, so a retry with another requestId still replays. A header-safe value (1 to 128 visible ASCII characters) is echoed as X-Request-Id; any other value is replaced by a server-chosen id.

TaskEventType.description: state_changed, output or artifact. The set is open: a later minor version may add types and optional fields. Clients ignore unknown optional fields and unknown types, while still checkpointing event cursors; strict validation against an older minor response schema is not supported. Existing fields forbidden for a known type cannot be repurposed on that type.

next_cursor.description: The last returned event cursor, never passing an event held back by limit. On an empty page, the requested position, or the durable retention floor if after was omitted. Required and never null, including when no events remain. No event may later become visible at or before this position.

semantic_revision.description: Semantic revision of the platform event the binding committed; an edited platform message binds a new revision instead of rewriting an existing binding.

sender_id.description: Authenticated sender identity the route was bound from; sender display names and chat titles grant no routing authority.

chat_id.description: Authenticated chat identity the route was bound from, when the platform has one.

thread_id.description: Authenticated thread identity the route was bound from, when the platform has one.

input_id.description: The input the Session admitted from this binding; present exactly while state is admitted.

segment_id.description: Stable identity of the delivery's first segment, the first entry of segments; only segments proven unsent are sent again, and an explicit resend keeps each carried identity under a new deliveryId. The authoritative per-segment view is segments.

ordinal.description: Position of the first segment (the singular segment_id) within the delivery, contiguous from 0.

provider_receipt.description: Representative opaque receipt the provider returned for this delivery; absent while the provider returned none, including a delivery reconciled out of unknown. The per-segment receipts are in segments.

segments.description: Every segment of the delivery in ordinal order, each with its own write-once provider receipt. The singular segment_id and ordinal name the first segment; this array is the authoritative per-segment view.

AutomationRunOutcome.description: firing is a claimed occurrence whose Harness answer is not recorded yet and is re-driven with bounded backoff; fired committed a run; skipped and missed never did; unknown is a claim whose answer stayed unobtainable past the retry bound and is never re-driven.

last_outcome.description: How the most recent probe decided: delivered fired a run with the output; quiet printed nothing; failed exited non-zero, timed out or could not start; blocked could not run on this Session; unknown is a probe the Runtime could not settle.

last_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the most recent probe.

quiet_since_delivery.description: Quiet probes since the last delivery.

consecutive_failures.description: Failed, blocked and unknown probes since the last quiet or delivered one.

last_error.description: What the last failing probe reported; absent while the streak is zero.

goal.description: At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes (measured as bytes, not code points; control characters are refused).

cron.description: Five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, digit, range, list and step atoms only.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name the deployment's tz database resolves.

prompt.description: At most 65536 UTF-8 bytes (measured as bytes); the final wrapped execution input must also fit the Session store's 65536-byte inline resource bound, so the effective prompt budget is tighter once escaping and framing are counted.

catch_up_limit.description: Set exactly for bounded catch-up: bounded requires one, any other policy clears it.

gate.description: A shell command the Workspace Runtime runs at each fire before any run is claimed: silence (exit 0, empty stdout) skips the fire, output wakes the Session with the output attached as data, a failure is recorded and never fires the prompt. At most 2048 UTF-8 bytes, no control characters, no unpaired surrogate, no shell wrapper such as bash -c, no part backgrounded with &. The output's block is reserved in the execution input, so a gated definition's prompt is about 32 KiB shorter than an ungated one's; a prompt too long only because of the gate answers 400 automation_gate_invalid. Null clears a committed gate; an absent field keeps it. Needs a Session whose tool profile declares Shell (409 automation_gate_unsupported otherwise).

gate.description: The definition's gate command; absent for a definition that fires every slot.

gate_status.description: The gate's recent outcomes; absent until the gate first ran, or for a definition without one.

id.description: The derived run id (arun_ plus the digest of the definition and occurrence); the same for a fired, skipped or missed occurrence.

slot.description: The canonical UTC slot instant of a scheduled occurrence; null for a manual run.

reason.description: overlap, count_limit, session_not_active, revision_stale or definition_retired for a skipped policy decision; gate_quiet, gate_failed, gate_blocked or gate_unknown for a fire the definition's gate withheld; answer_unobtainable for an unknown one; a definitive Harness refusal settles skipped carrying its own error code verbatim (invalid_automation_operation, automation_mode_disabled, automation_count_limit or automation_operation_conflict); absent otherwise.

state.description: The run's task state once the run committed; null until its record is visible.

A node that cannot be read, no longer admits the actor or holds another registration's marker leaves it for administrator review, and a new browser draft does not release it. failed releases the directory if the registration reserved it. replayed=true identifies an existing operation returned by a repeated key or a query.

SessionRecovery.description: Separate from Session lifecycle and Turn outcome. ready requires affirmative native input settlement and an admissible continuation boundary with no active Java Turn or blocking debt. Actions are authorization-scoped hints, checked again by their mutations. A new-Session action opens an editable text handoff and grants no additional Workspace permission. A cold or unreadable terminal Turn may advertise a proof-checked cleanup recheck while remaining operator_required with nextTurnAllowed=false; only affirmative native evidence after that mutation can establish readiness.

ManagedPermissionRules.description: Session-scoped portable permission-rules/1. Each rule must be trimmed, nonempty, free of control characters, and at most 512 UTF-8 bytes. At most 32 unique strings per list, 64 across all lists and 8192 UTF-8 bytes of compact JSON. Tool names and aliases match whole tools; MCP names may end with a wildcard. Bash/Shell/run_shell_command/monitor command globs and WebFetch/web_fetch(domain:host) are supported; file-path specifiers and arbitrary tool predicates are rejected. Deny takes precedence over ask, then allow, in every mode. Rules do not provide filesystem or process isolation.

UserMessageCommand.description: submit queues input; edit only changes queued input. withdraw removes queued input or explicitly discards recovery_blocked input without replaying it. Unknown delivery may already have reached the original Turn: discarding does not undo it, preserves late durable receipts and keeps the queue paused until resume. In-flight claimed input remains immutable. Commands replay the actor-scoped recorded result before checking new-work availability.
